title: Unique Paths
statement: A robot sits at the top-left corner of an m x n grid. It can only move either down or right at each step, and it is trying to reach the bottom-right corner. Given the two integers m and n (grid rows and columns, both >= 1), return the number of distinct paths from the top-left to the bottom-right corner.
hints: The number of ways to reach a cell only depends on the number of ways to reach the cell above it and the cell to its left, since those are the only two directions you can arrive from.
Build a 2-D table dp where dp[i][j] is the number of paths from the start to cell (i, j); the entire first row and first column are all 1 (only one way to walk straight along an edge).
Initialize dp as an m by n grid of 1s; for i from 1 to m-1 and j from 1 to n-1, set dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]; return dp[m-1][n-1].
